Privacy policy

Last updated: 12 November 2026 (version 2026-11-12)

Forge is a training app made by Ashley Barton in the United Kingdom. Ashley Barton is the data controller for the information described here. Contact: barton.at@gmail.com.

This policy explains what Forge stores, where, why, and how to delete it.

Your Forge account

Forge needs a free account, created with Sign in with Apple or Google when you first open the app. (Before version 0.1 build 34 you could use Forge without one.) Your phone also keeps its own copy of your data, with up to 7 daily backups in the app's own storage.

  • What we receive from Apple or Google: an account identifier, your email address (with Sign in with Apple you can choose to hide it), and your name if you share it. We never see your Apple or Google password.
  • What is saved to your account:
    • your profile: goal, training days, session length, equipment and experience
    • logged workouts
    • saved workouts and folders (My workouts)
    • your plan and AI coach plans
    • injuries and how they're progressing
    • HYROX race details
    • your settings
  • Why: so your history is never lost, you can sign in on a new phone, and the AI coach can work without your own API key.
  • Where: Forge's server is run by Supabase on Amazon Web Services in London (eu-west-2). Data is encrypted in transit and at rest. Each account can only read its own data.
  • Injuries and training data are health data. We only store them in your account with your explicit agreement. You give it with the switch shown before you sign in, and we record the date and the version of this policy you agreed to. You can withdraw it at any time by deleting your account.
  • Your workouts in progress, Apple Health settings and readiness scores stay on your phone.

Apple Health

If you allow it, Forge reads:

  • workouts, runs, running distance, steps and active energy
  • heart rate, heart rate variability, resting heart rate, VO₂ max and how fast your heart rate drops after a workout
  • sleep, breathing rate, wrist temperature and blood oxygen
  • date of birth and biological sex, to set your heart-rate zones and fitness age
  • weight, body fat and lean mass; protein, caffeine and alcoholic drinks; time in daylight and mindful minutes
  • menstrual flow, only if you turn on cycle tracking

It saves your finished workouts to Apple Health. On Apple Watch, Forge records the workouts you do with it (heart rate and calories) and saves them to Apple Health.

Apple Health data is used on your phone to work out recovery, exertion, sleep, training load and fitness age. It is never uploaded to Forge's server and never used for advertising. It is only shared as described under "The AI coach", and only if you turn that on. Cycle data is never sent anywhere. If you export your heart-rate data from the Recovery screen, the file goes only where you choose to send it.

The AI coach

When you ask the AI coach to plan a week or a 6-week block, Forge sends Anthropic (the maker of Claude) the information needed to write the plan:

  • your profile and equipment
  • active injuries
  • recent training, up to the last 3 weeks
  • any note you add
  • if you turn on Share with the AI coach (off by default): today's recovery, exertion target, sleep, training load, fitness age, weight, protein, and the habits most linked with your recovery. Cycle data is never sent.

When you paste a workout that Forge can't fully read, it sends the pasted text to Anthropic to read it.

  • With an account, these requests go through Forge's server, which checks your monthly allowance and passes them to Anthropic. Forge's server keeps only a count of requests and their size, not what was sent or the answer.
  • Anthropic processes this data under its commercial terms and data processing terms, which do not allow it to train models on it. Anthropic may process data in the United States, under the safeguards in those terms.
  • If you use your own Claude API key instead of an account, requests go straight from your phone to Anthropic under your own agreement with Anthropic.

Pastes Forge can't read

When a plan you paste doesn't read properly (lines Forge can't read, missing sets or reps, Claude needed to help, or you correct what Forge read before adding it), Forge sends a report to Forge's server so the reader can be fixed. A report contains:

  • the pasted text, with email addresses, phone numbers, links and your name taken out
  • what Forge read from it, what was unclear, and any changes you made before adding it
  • the version of the app

It doesn't contain your name, email or account. The server keeps a one-way code made from your account, which can't be turned back into it, so we can count how many different people hit the same problem and limit how many reports one account sends. If a plan you paste mentions an injury, that text is included, so we ask for your explicit agreement: with the switch shown before you sign in, or, if you signed in before reports existed, with a question on the Today screen.

Reports are read by Ashley Barton, and by Claude (Anthropic), which works out the cause when a report arrives and helps fix the reader. We get an email about each new report through Resend, with what went wrong and the lines Forge couldn't read, not the whole paste. Reports are deleted after 90 days. You can turn reports off in More › Send pastes Forge can't read; any reports still waiting on your phone are then deleted.

Who we share data with

We share data only with the services that run Forge:

  • Supabase: hosting and database (London).
  • Anthropic: the AI coach, only when you use it, and Claude to help us fix pastes Forge can't read.
  • Resend: emails us about pastes Forge can't read.
  • Apple and Google: sign-in only.

We don't sell data, show adverts, or use analytics or tracking tools.

Lawful bases (UK GDPR)

  • Running your account and syncing your data: contract.
  • Health information (injuries, training, recovery): explicit consent.
  • Reports of pastes Forge can't read: explicit consent, which you can withdraw in More.
  • Keeping the service secure and enforcing fair-use limits on the AI coach: legitimate interests.

How long we keep it

  • While you have an account: we keep your data until you delete it.
  • When you delete your account: everything stored with it is deleted from the server straight away. Server backups that may contain it are overwritten within 7 days.
  • Reports of pastes Forge can't read: 90 days, then deleted. They aren't linked to your account, so deleting your account doesn't delete them; they're deleted at 90 days either way.
  • Server security logs: these may include IP addresses and are kept by Supabase for a short period.

Your rights

You can:

  • See and export your data: More › Backup & import exports everything as a file.
  • Correct it: edit it in the app.
  • Delete it: More › Account › Delete account deletes your account and everything in it. More › Reset all data clears this phone.
  • Withdraw consent: delete your account, or turn off paste reports in More.
  • Ask a question or make a request: email barton.at@gmail.com. We'll reply within one month.

If you're unhappy with how we handle your data, you can complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ico.org.uk).

Children

Forge isn't intended for children under 13.

Changes

If this policy changes in a way that affects what we do with your data, the app will tell you, and ask you to agree again where it needs your consent.
